correctness.rationale: For all real v and real symmetric trace-free 3×3 A, exact Gaussian Wick and radial moments give ∫f⁴=9p²/5+18pq/7+15q²/7+16|Av|²/35, p=|v|²/3, q=2 tr(A²)/15. Newton trace identity tr(A⁴)=tr(A²)²/2 is exact in dimension three. The trace-zero eigenvalue inequality 0≤|Av|²≤2|v|²tr(A²)/3 and explicit square completions prove both deficits and force all equality cases, with no missing zero modes since optimal energy proportions are strictly positive. Standalone standard-library checker performed exact 150 rational configurations and independent quadrature; symbolic 8-parameter polynomial identity also independently checked during this scientific review. The analytical proof, not finite tests, establishes universality.

originality.rationale: Primary literature on norm comparisons and reverse Hölder inequalities does not imply the exact mixed H1⊕H2 bounds. Closest published pure H2 sharp theorem has constant 15/7, while new sharp mixed endpoints straddle it and involve nonzero H1, with orientation-dependent |Av|². Specific equivalent/stronger-source checks and material reads are recorded below; older inaccessible or unindexed analogues remain a risk.
residual_risks: The 1981 Stanton–Weinstein full text was not read; the abstract supports only a fixed-degree comparison, not a whole-document noncoverage conclusion.
The exact constants and mixed dipole/quadrupole patterns may have been expressed in older invariant-theory or physical multipole literature under different terminology.
Negative database and full-web queries do not prove absolute mathematical uniqueness.

value.rationale: The first nonconstant spherical band \(\mathcal H_1\oplus\mathcal H_2\) is an intrinsically defined eight-dimensional harmonic approximation space. Both sharp moment endpoints require a nonzero mixture; the lower forces a null-axis dipole with traceless rank-two quadrupole, the upper forces alignment with a zonal quadrupole. Distinct extremal geometries, full attainable range and exact nonnegative stability remainders solve a naturally motivated finite-dimensional norm problem, rather than just evaluating a single special polynomial.
